newsitem.title: JAPAN: Typhoon may disrupt shipping at Okinawa refineries.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon may disrupt shipping at Okinawa refineries.

text.p: Refineries on Japan's southern island of Okinawa were expecting possible disruptions to loading and discharge operations by an approaching typhoon, plant officials said on Tuesday.
Production at the facilities, however, was likely to be unaffected and the plants were not expecting crude oil shortages, the officials said.
Okinawa is home to Nansei Sekiyu KK's 100,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery and Okinawa Sekiyu Seisei's 110,000 bpd facility.
An official at Nansei Sekiyu's plant said that a scheduled lifting of C grade fuel oil had been cancelled on Tuesday, but that refining operations at the plant were unaffected.
A spokesman at Okinawa Sekiyu Seisei said the plant was taking standard precautions ahead of the typhoon's arrival but that refining operations were normal at present.
The refinery is expecting the arrival of a very large crude carrier (VLCC) loaded with crude oil on August 9, a spokesman said.

Typhoon Tina, expected to pack 100 mile per hour winds when it hits Okinawa late Wednesday, was forecast to reach the southwest island of Kyushu by Thursday, according to independent forecaster Weather Services Corp.
Okinawa Sekiyu Seisei is a wholly owned subsidiary of Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd.
